surprises.head: Dallas hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Dallas’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 38, against their usual 99 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: The Stars pour it on late
paras: Tyler Seguin got the scoring started for the Stars midway through the first, but Matthew Schaefer tied it 1-1 for the Islanders a little over two minutes later. Jason Robertson put the Stars back ahead 2-1, 49 seconds later. Kyle Palmieri made it 2-2 for the Islanders early in the second, and Justin Hryckowian restored the Stars’ lead on the power play midway through the period. Brayden Schenn tied it up for the Islanders late in the period, but the Islanders didn’t score again. Wyatt Johnston put the Stars back ahead 4-3 early in the third. Robertson and Mikko Rantanen scored a little over three minutes apart midway through the period to make it 6-3, and the Islanders never had an answer.

The Stars carried the play, outshooting the Islanders 38-20, and got the result to match. Jake Oettinger made 17 saves for the Stars, and Ilya Sorokin allowed six goals on 38 shots. By our Swing measure, Lian Bichsel had the best night of anyone. The Stars improved to 7-3-1, third in the Central, while the Isles fell to 5-4-2, fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Stars are rolling: five straight wins.
The Islanders’ five-game point streak is over.
Jason Robertson scored twice more against the Islanders, and has eight goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Mikko Rantanen has a point in five straight games.
